 79: Host binding table (locks the D1 nonce source, the D5 arrival source, and the D2 host session key per host; every turn token is still minted by the server). Rules common to all hosts:
 80: - Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256. Equal-field rule (copilot and classic cline, whose nonce hashes event fields with no per-message id): under `turn-open.lock`, a new prompt-hook invocation whose nonce already has a failsafe mint record or a `pending-<nonce>` turn in that host session, or whose mint returns `merged`, cannot be told apart from a separate message with equal session, timestamp, and prompt, so it mints and binds nothing and the host session fails closed under D6 exactly as the bridge does for an unattributable record (`unsupportedSince: { causeNonce, causeOperation: prompt_hook, reason: indistinguishable_arrival }` with the session-level envelope; every session-log verb then reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until the session ends, except that writes for a turn already open at that moment go to the plugin failsafe under the unsupported-session failsafe rule, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001; its open turns are listed at the next SessionStart). A network retry or failsafe replay of a stored mint record is a drain of that record, not a new invocation, and reuses its nonce without failing closed.
 81: - Unsupported-session rule (D6; operator option 1 of 2026-10-10): every check that makes a host session report `turn_logging_unsupported` after one of its requests was delivered records `unsupportedSince` with the session-level envelope in `turn-state.yaml` in the same atomic replace that makes the session unsupported, with `reason` set to that check's code: `queue_removal_ambiguous` (bridge), `indistinguishable_arrival` (equal-field rule), `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` (an unknown queue operation, a record missing a required field, or a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset`), `duplicate_prompt_hook` (the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check starts failing; the first verb or hook in that host session that observes it records it), or, for any other D6 check, its own reason code; plus `causeOffset` or `causeNonce` where the cause has one, else `detectedAtUtc`. Whatever the reason, the unsupported-session failsafe of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 then applies: writes for a turn delivered and still in progress at that moment are captured, and every mint and every other write is refused. The state lasts until the host session ends, or until a SessionStart clears its cause where the cause's own rule allows (the bridge restarting on a valid transcript); the captured records drain at that SessionStart. A host that is unsupported from its first event mints nothing, has no open turn, and records no `unsupportedSince`.
 82: - Host session key: read from the verb's own invocation context as listed per host. Long-lived processes (stdio MCP servers, the arrival bridge itself) never trust a key captured at spawn time, because a host may change the session in place (Claude Code `/clear`; resume without an explicit id keeps the startup id in long-lived subprocesses per the Claude Code env-var reference); they resolve the key per call by the live-session rule.
 83: - Queued-message arrival on every host (D5, D6): P0.2 records, per host, whether a message sent while a turn is running reaches an arrival mechanism at enqueue. Where the prompt event itself fires at enqueue, it is the arrival mechanism; where it fires only at processing time, the host's transcript or queue event is used through an arrival adapter with the same `queued`/`delivered`/`withdrawn` lifecycle as the Claude Code bridge; where neither exists, the host is unsupported for turn logging (`turn_logging_unsupported`).
 84: - Live-session rule (D2 fallback): a host session is live from its first mint until its session-end event (Claude Code `SessionEnd`, including reason `clear`; Codex `SessionEnd`; Copilot session end; cline-v2 and opencode session close) marks `sessions/<key>/ended.yaml`, or until 12 hours without a mint or verb (the idle rule writes `ended.yaml` with `reason: idle`; a session-end event writes `reason: session_end`). A verb without its own key binds to the single live session of its agent in the workspace (`host_session_inferred`), and is refused with `host_session_unknown` (none live) or `host_session_ambiguous` (several live) unless it passes the trusted (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair of C5.
 85: - claude-code: nonce: the bridge's `q-` enqueue nonce (the bridge is the only minter, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009); hook key payload `session_id`; verb key env `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` read at verb start in shell, PowerShell, and hook subprocesses (equals `session_id`; those subprocesses see the updated value after `/clear`); stdio MCP verbs use the live-session rule; payloads carrying `agent_id` are subagent events (system events, no turn); the subagent's own Bash and PowerShell verbs carry the parent's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and bind to the parent's write target; stop uses payload `stop_hook_active`. Arrival bridge (D5), the only minter on claude-code (known-good single source of truth: the host transcript is one ordered log written by one producer, so the bridge needs no key shared with the hook, which the host does not provide: Claude Code's `queue-operation` records carry no `promptId` although its user records do): started by SessionStart with the payload `transcript_path`, it applies `queue-operation` lines in file order. Every `enqueue` takes a queue position, so FIFO `dequeue` stays exact. An `enqueue` whose `content` the system-event classifier marks as a system event is added as `{ kind: system, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued }` with the session-level envelope `{ workspacePath, agent, mcpSessionId, hostSessionKey }` (it has no nonce or requestId, and none is ever invented for it) and is never minted. An `enqueue` whose `content` the classifier accepts as a user request: mint with nonce `q-` + SHA-256(`session_id` LF the record's starting byte offset in the transcript LF enqueue `timestamp` LF `content`) truncated to 62 hex characters (the offset is unique per record and identical on replay, so two distinct records with equal timestamp and content get two nonces), and add `{ kind: request, requestId, nonce, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued, stateOffset, mintedAtUtc }` with the root-id envelope to the queue in `sessions/<key>/turn-state.yaml`. `dequeue` (no content) removes the head of the host session's `queued` entries: a `kind: request` head becomes `delivered` and the write target; a `kind: system` head is removed and delivers nothing. `remove` and `popAll` records that match a `kind: system` entry drop it without a turn. `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`: the `queued` entry whose `promptSha256` equals the record's `content` hash (both written by the same producer) becomes `delivered` and the write target when exactly one queued entry has that hash. `remove` with any other or no reason: the matching `queued` entry becomes `withdrawn` when exactly one queued entry has that content hash. `popAll`: when, for every content line it carries, the number of lines with that content equals the number of queued entries with that content hash, those entries become `withdrawn`. Fail-closed rule (D6): a `remove` carries `commandUuid` and `deliveryId` (Claude Code 2.1.293), which also appear on the delivered message's `queued_command` attachment, but `enqueue` and `dequeue` carry no key shared with it, so a `remove` that matches two or more queued entries, or a `popAll` that carries fewer lines of a content than there are queued entries with that content, cannot be attributed (a `popAll` whose line count equals the matching entry count withdraws them all, because every candidate is withdrawn). The bridge never guesses: at the first such record it stops before it without advancing `appliedThroughOffset`, sets `turn-state.yaml` `unsupportedSince: { causeOffset, causeOperation, reason: queue_removal_ambiguous }`, and from then on every session-log verb in that host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until the session ends, except that writes for a turn already open at that moment go to the plugin failsafe (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001). Turns that are open at that moment are left exactly as they are on the server, the stop gate blocks on each only until the model's close of it is captured in the plugin failsafe and then warns `queue_removal_ambiguous` listing them (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001), and the next SessionStart for the agent lists them with their original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pairs for closing through the trusted recovery flow (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC006). P0.2 records the `remove` identity fields; the bridge never uses them to pair with an `enqueue`. Only `queue-operation` lines are arrival records; every other record type is ignored by design. A `queue-operation` with an unknown operation or a missing required field is never skipped: the bridge stops before it without advancing `appliedThroughOffset`, records warning `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` and, after a delivered request, `unsupportedSince` with that reason and the record's `causeOffset` in the same atomic replace (unsupported-session rule), and the host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb (D6) until a verified adapter handles that shape, while writes for a turn already open go to the plugin failsafe (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001). Each record's state change and the advance of `appliedThroughOffset` past it are one atomic replace of `turn-state.yaml` (temp file, flush, rename, under `turn-open.lock`); records that start below `appliedThroughOffset` are skipped, so a restart never re-applies a record; the server mint for `enqueue` happens before that replace and is idempotent (same nonce, `merged`). Records are applied by whichever process holds `turn-open.lock`: the bridge, or a session-log verb, which first records the transcript length at the moment the invocation starts and, after taking the lock, applies every pending record that ends at or before that length, never a record appended later, before it binds (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC006), so a verb started after a `dequeue` line was written binds to that request, and a `dequeue` appended after the verb started never retargets it (D2). name: Triage Reporting
description: "Use when your agent discovers an incidental bug while working on another task and should submit it to MCP Server triage without changing focus. Triggers: 'triage', '/triage', 'submit a triage report', 'report an incidental bug', 'file this bug to triage', 'triage status'."
version: 0.1.0

# Triage Reporting

Use MCP Server triage for an incidental bug discovered while doing other work. Do not use triage for the user's active requested fix, assigned TODO, or current implementation target; fix that directly or track it through the normal TODO and requirements workflow.

Submit the report, then continue the current task. Do not expect immediate resolution, research, or TODO creation. Intake only returns the accepted queue state; background triage later groups reports, researches them, and may create a `BUG-TRIAGE-###` backlog TODO.

MCP Server-related reports, including MCP Server plugin bugs, are grouped into the registered `McpServer` workspace when that workspace exists. If no `McpServer` workspace is registered, the report stays in the submitting workspace.

## Tools

- Use `triage_report` to submit an incidental bug report.
- Native MCP clients may use `triage_status`; plugin/REPL callers must use schema-valid `workflow.triage.getReport`, `workflow.triage.getGroup`, or `workflow.triage.queryGroups` for status inspection.

## Report Shape

Include enough evidence for later research without leaving the active task:

- `title`: short problem statement.
- `summary`: observed failure and why it matters.
- `component`: product area, package, or plugin name.
- `affectedPaths`: relevant paths when known.
- `affectedSymbols`: relevant methods, commands, or API names when known.
- `errorSignature`: stable error text, status code, or exception type when known.
- `dedupeKey`: stable key when the same bug may be reported again.
- `evidence`: compact command output or reproduction context.

## REPL Example

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260625T120000Z-triage-report
  method: workflow.triage.report
  params:
    title: Plugin wrapper hides triage_report validation errors
    summary: The wrapper exits with success after a triage_report validation failure, masking the error.
    component: mcpserver-plugin
    affectedPaths:
      - lib/repl-invoke.ps1
    errorSignature: triage_validation_hidden
    reporterAgent: <your-agent>
```

After a successful response, record the returned `reportId`, `groupId`, `status`, and `quietDeadlineUtc` only if useful for the current audit trail, then continue the current task.

## PowerShell Object-Safe Example

When using the plugin PowerShell surface, prefer the exported shim helpers and `-ParamsObject` so the wrapper serializes the YAML payload:

```powershell
Import-Module (Join-Path $env:MCP_PLUGIN_ROOT 'lib/McpPluginShim.psm1') -Force
$params = New-McpTriageReportParams `
    -Title 'Plugin wrapper hides triage validation errors' `
    -Summary 'workflow.triage.report failures are not visible to the agent.' `
    -Component 'mcpserver-plugin' `
    -AffectedPaths @('lib/repl-invoke.ps1') `
    -ErrorSignature 'triage_validation_hidden' `
    -ReporterAgent '<your-agent>'
& (Join-Path $env:MCP_PLUGIN_ROOT 'lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1') -Command Invoke -Method workflow.triage.report -ParamsObject $params
```

Use `New-McpTriageGetReportParams`, `New-McpTriageGetGroupParams`, and `New-McpTriageQueryGroupsParams` for object-safe status inspection through `workflow.triage.getReport`, `workflow.triage.getGroup`, and `workflow.triage.queryGroups`.

# Adversarial review and deploy (global, permanent)

**Locked 2026-08-12 by operator.** Applies in every session and every repo. Not optional. Not McpServer-only.

## Every result of every request

1. **Adversarial validation.** Independently validate via a hostile reviewer sub-agent (`hostile-validator` skill / `spawn_subagent`). Self-check alone is not validation.
2. **UTC timestamp.** Every result is timestamped in UTC.
3. **Display review failures.** Every FAIL and UNKNOWN from the adversarial review is shown to the user. Never bury failures.
4. **Accuracy and completeness ratings.** Every result includes both an **accuracy** rating and a **completeness** rating (numeric scale with short justification).

## Hostile validation score gate (locked 2026-09-10)

**Effective immediately:** a hostile validation passes only when both its accuracy score and completeness score are at least 98 percent. Any individual score below 98 percent is a failure. `OverallVerdict` must be `DISAGREE` when either score is below 98, even if the claim FAIL and UNKNOWN counts are both zero.

A result with either score below 98 cannot authorize a goal, TODO, requirement, or plan done-state change. The parent must display every sub-98 score as a failure, remediate the deficiency, and rerun hostile validation before acceptance.

This applies to the current in-flight review and all future hostile reviews. It supersedes any earlier practice that accepted an `AGREE` verdict with a lower numeric score. The 98 percent rule is an acceptance threshold, not a target reviewers may game or inflate.

## Hostile validation mandatory scope (locked 2026-08-13)

**Operator directive (verbatim intent):** Hostile Validation must test for **workspace rule violations**, **requirement violations**, and the **current plan holistically**, **in addition to** the requested validation.

Applies every hostile run, every workspace. Not optional. Not limited to McpServer use-case UI checks.

Mandatory attack surfaces on every run:

1. **Requested validation** — every implementer claim (pass/done/green/fixed, SHAs, test counts, receipts).
2. **Workspace rules** — honesty, receipts, MCP-only TODO/session/requirements storage when the workspace uses MCP, lab PowerShell/no-Python. **Byrd Development Process v4 and related directives pertain only to code and documentation in the scope of implementing the project.** Phase-order (requirements drive tests; tests before implementation) is caught by a hostile review **between phases** of plan implementation. Do not FAIL B2 solely by comparing FR `createdAt` to test/implementation file times after the slice is written. Do not apply Byrd TDD to user-directed ops.
3. **Requirements** — apply to **project requirement work** only (product features, implementation, claimed-complete plan steps). FR/TR/TEST/AC/mappings required there. Missing FR/TR/AC for claimed-complete implementation work is FAIL.
   **Do not apply surface C to user-directed general actions** (uninstall an obsolete package, device backup, ADB pair, screenshot, operator-named restore/copy). Those are not project requirements. "No FR/TR for this uninstall" is not a valid FAIL. Classify the work on the receipt. If a turn mixes ops and product work, FAIL C only on the product slice. See `hostile-ops-vs-requirements.md`.
4. **Current plan holistically** — when the implementer claims plan-step completion: plan DoD, blockers, amendments, exit criteria. A user-directed ops action does not have to satisfy an unrelated product plan DoD unless they claimed that plan step done.

**OverallVerdict=AGREE** only if all *applicable* surfaces of (1)+(2)+(3)+(4) PASS. Surface C is N/A (not a FAIL) for class-2 operator actions. Parent agents must not under-scope the brief to code-only claims on class-1 work; if they do, the hostile sub-agent expands and still evaluates applicable (2)+(3)+(4).

**add-profile first:** Hostile validator must execute the `add-profile` skill before beginning its validation work (every run, including resume). Receipt must record that it ran.

Authoritative skill text: `~/.grok/skills/hostile-validator/SKILL.md`.

## Adversarial reviewer session-log obligation

**All adversarial reviewers must create complete MCP Session Log turns for every review performed.**

Required lifecycle (plugin `workflow.sessionlog.*` / equivalent, never hand-edit log files):

1. bootstrap (if needed)
2. openSession (dedicated review session or clear review turn on agent session)
3. beginTurn
4. appendDialog / appendActions (integer `order` values)
5. completeTurn or failTurn
6. Prove persistence (`queryHistory` or equivalent server proof in the hostile receipt)

A review without a complete session-log turn is **incomplete**, even if claim verdicts would otherwise pass.

## HV jsonl and full session-log body (locked 2026-09-10)

**Operator directive (verbatim intent):** HV requests must have request and response logged as jsonl files from now on. The results of HV validation must be saved in their entirety to the MCP Session Log.

Every HV launch writes two durable jsonl files (request as sent; response as the full `--json` or equivalent stream). Do not leave them only in Temp/scratch. Workspace path: `docs/receipts/hv/{utc}-{gate}.request.jsonl` and `.response.jsonl`; otherwise `%USERPROFILE%\.grok\hv-receipts\`.

The reviewer's MCP session-log turn must store the **entire** HV result: full verdict prose, every finding, scores, OverallVerdict, VERDICT JSON, and jsonl paths. A one-line AGREE or a paraphrase is not the result. Missing jsonl or a summarized session-log body makes the HV incomplete; incomplete HV cannot AGREE and cannot authorize done.

See [[hv-jsonl-and-session-log]].

## Status report contract after validation

Parent status reports that claim pass/done/green/complete must include:

- Receipt path
- `OverallVerdict` (`AGREE` or `DISAGREE`)
- PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN counts
- Full FAIL list
- Adversarial sessionId + turn requestId when session-log was required

If the receipt is missing or `OverallVerdict` is `DISAGREE`, **do not** claim step completion and **do not** change a goal, plan step, or MCP TODO to `done: true`. Hostile AGREE is required before any goal-state change. See `hostile-on-goal-state.md`.

## Deploy: Nuke only, never manual

When deploying McpServer (and other lab services that ship with Nuke targets):

- **Use Nuke** (for McpServer: elevated `./build.ps1 UpdateService` as documented on the target).
- **Never** hand-copy binaries into `C:\ProgramData\...`, never ad-hoc `Stop-Service`/`Start-Service` + `Copy-Item` deploy scripts as a substitute for Nuke.
- Manual file edits of live config may be acceptable when they are the intended change (e.g. `appsettings.yaml` provider flags) and Nuke restore/preserve rules keep them; binary deploy still goes through Nuke.

148 ### Step 4 - Update Turn
149 
150 To record interpretation, response summary, tags, and referenced files during work:
151 
152 ```yaml
153 type: request
154 payload:
155   requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-update-001
156   method: workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn
157   params:
158     response: Created TokenService and JwtValidator classes
159     interpretation: User wants JWT authentication with token generation and validation
160     tokenCount: 1250
161     tags:
162       - feature
163       - security
164       - FR-AUTH-001
165     contextList:
166       - src/Services/TokenService.cs
167       - src/Services/JwtValidator.cs
168 ```
169 
170 ### Step 5 - Append Dialog
171 
172 To record reasoning steps, tool calls, observations, and decisions as the work progresses:
173 
174 ```yaml
175 type: request
176 payload:
177   requestId: req-20260409T120004Z-dialog-001
178   method: workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog
179   params:
180     dialogItems:
181       - timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:04Z
182         role: model
183         content: Analyzing authentication requirements and existing patterns...
184         category: reasoning
185       - timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:05Z
186         role: model
187         content: |
188           Decision: Use HS256 for JWT signing.
189           Rationale: Symmetric key simplifies key management for this internal service.
190           Alternatives: RS256 adds key distribution complexity without benefit here.
191         category: decision
192 ```
193 
194 Valid `category` values: `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `observation`, `decision`.
195 
196 Valid `role` values: `model`, `tool`, `system`, `user`.
197 
198 ### Step 6 - Append Actions
199 
200 To record file operations and other work artifacts:
201 
202 ```yaml
203 type: request
204 payload:
205   requestId: req-20260409T120005Z-actions-001
206   method: workflow.sessionlog.appendActions
207   params:
208     actions:
209       - order: 1
210         description: Created TokenService with JWT generation
211         type: create
212         status: completed
213         filePath: src/Services/TokenService.cs
214       - order: 2
215         description: Created JwtValidator for token validation
216         type: create
217         status: completed
218         filePath: src/Services/JwtValidator.cs
219       - order: 3
220         description: Chose HS256 for JWT signing (internal service, symmetric key)
221         type: design_decision
222         status: completed
223         filePath: ""
224 ```
225 
226 Standard action `type` values: `edit`, `create`, `delete`, `design_decision`, `commit`, `pr_comment`, `issue_comment`, `web_reference`, `dependency_add`.
227 
228 `actions[].order` must be an unquoted integer (`order: 1`, never `order: "1"`).
229 
230 ### Step 7 - Complete Turn
231 
232 To finalize a turn as successfully completed (immutable after this call):
233 
234 ```yaml
235 type: request
236 payload:
237   requestId: req-20260409T120006Z-complete-001
238   method: workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn
239   params:
240     response: |
241       JWT authentication implemented:
242       - TokenService generates HS256-signed tokens
243       - JwtValidator validates and extracts claims
244       - Services registered in Startup.cs
245       - All unit tests passing
246 ```
247 
248 ### Failing a Turn
249 
250 To mark a turn as failed with an error description:
251 
252 ```yaml
253 type: request
254 payload:
255   requestId: req-20260409T120007Z-fail-001
256   method: workflow.sessionlog.failTurn
257   params:
258     errorMessage: Unable to complete - missing System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt package
259     errorCode: dependency_missing
260 ```
261 
262 Both `completeTurn` and `failTurn` produce an immutable terminal state. No further `updateTurn`, `appendDialog`, or `appendActions` calls are allowed on a completed or failed turn.
